headline: WIRED says data centres have become a campaign issue in US races for Senate, House and governor ahead of the 3 November midterm elections.
score_reason: Kept at 5: an 11 Oct 2026 column with some outside research, but the key judgement is the columnist's.
importance_line: It matters to voters and candidates in states with planned data centres, then to developers, because moratorium promises and local ballot measures could change where large data centres can be built, but the column is one writer's reading of the races and not a forecast of results.
summary: WIRED reports in its weekly Power Play column that opposition to data centres crosses party lines and has become a weapon in the 3 Nov midterm elections, with Democrat Sherrod Brown attacking Ohio Senator Jon Husted over data centres and energy bills, at least 20 candidates in the 36 governor races promising some kind of moratorium, according to research by Multistate, and voters in eight states facing more than 30 local ballot measures, over half of them in Ohio. The columnist judges the issue strong enough that it could swing tight races and notes that Texas Governor Greg Abbott has gone from welcoming data centres to a de facto freeze on permits in under a year.
notes: Column (analysis mixed with reporting). Could sit under POL; kept ENE per the chunk default.
